subject: Anchorage - Dedicated fleet sizing & peering considerations

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Anchorage: fleet sizing + peering questions

Hi Maya / Anchorage procurement team —

Thanks again for the time on Friday. To make our Dedicated proposal tight I have a couple of follow-ups on expected workload shape so we can map to GPU slab types and peering/topology: 

- Typical tokens per request (median and 95th) for the LLM endpoint you plan to run?
- Concurrent steady-state TPS and expected hourly spike multiplier (e.g., 3x during batch jobs)
- P95 latency SLO target for user-facing calls (you mentioned 150ms in the demo — can you confirm?)
- Any region constraints / VPC peering or interconnect requirements for low-latency egress?

I've attached a first-draft capacity workbook (anchorage_capacity_model_v1.xlsx) with a few sizing scenarios (quantized 8-bit vs FP16, and 2x/3x headroom). If you can share the traffic profile I can run a more precise tokens-per-second->GPU-slab mapping and suggest peering/egress placement.

Proposed next step: 30-min call Tuesday to review the model and finalize the Dedicated slab recommendation.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Hi Kimberly —

Appreciate the follow-up. Quick answers below — happy to provide logs if that helps.

- Tokens per request: median ~320 tokens, 95th ~1,800 tokens (we have longer batch summarization jobs).
- Steady-state TPS: ~12 requests/sec during business hours; night batch windows push effective token throughput to ~60 TPS-equivalent for ~30 minutes (happens ~2x/week).
- Latency SLO: user-facing endpoints we want p95 <= 200ms; admin/batch can tolerate higher.
- Region: US only for now; low-latency peering via a dedicated interconnect would be ideal — we can share our VPC details via the procurement contact.

Cc'ing procurement to coordinate any network paperwork.

Best,
Maya

Kimberly / Ben —

Thanks for sharing Maya's numbers. Quick notes mapping to our internal slab matrix: 

- Median 320 tokens at 12 r/s is modest; the weekly 60 TPS-equivalent spike with 1,800-token tails is the main driver for headroom and KV cache sizing.
- For user-facing p95 <= 200ms I recommend we target a mix: quantized 8-bit variant for cost efficiency + a small FP16 reserve for the long-tail jobs (can failover via routing policy).
- Network: peering/interconnect reduces egress tail — recommend proposing a colocated placement in region-us-west-2 with direct peering to Anchorage to shave ~30-50ms off tail latencies.

Priyom — can you run a quick tokens/sec -> GPUs needed sketch (include KV cache warmup and cold start risk) and flag any constraints if they use the larger 1,800-token batch flows?

- Karthik

Karthik / team —

I ran a quick modeling pass using the attached workbook assumptions. Summary (rounded):

- Baseline inference footprint (quantized 8-bit, 7B-ish model profile):
  - Median 320 tokens @12 r/s -> ~3.8 kTokens/sec steady -> comfortably handled by 1 slab (4x A100 equivalent lanes) with ~1.8x steady headroom.
- Spike scenario (60 TPS-equivalent, 95th 1,800 tokens):
  - Peak token throughput ~108 kTokens/sec during spike window -> requires ~8 slabs of quantized 8-bit to maintain p95 <= 200ms assuming KV cache warm.
  - If KV cache is cold, the cold-start penalty increases p95 significantly; recommend pre-warming policy during scheduled batch windows.
- FP16 reserve: keep 2 FP16-capable slabs to offload long-tail heavy requests (reduces latency variance for 1,800-token batches).
- Proposed safety buffer: +25% slab cushion for sustained weeks to absorb unexpected adoption growth and model variant rollouts.

Network/peering notes:
- colocated placement in us-west-2 with direct interconnect reduces median+tail by ~30ms in our tests; if Anchorage can accept a single-region placement, this is easiest.

Actionable recommendation to include in quote: 
- Start with 4 quantized slabs reserved (handles steady load + modest headroom) + autoscale policy to add up to 10 quantized slabs for spikes, with a 2-slab FP16 fallback pool for heavy batch requests.
- SLO mapping: commit p95 <= 200ms for user-facing routes; allow 500-800ms for admin/batch and document automatic fallback triggers.

Link to the detailed sheet: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3Cexample (sheet: anchorage_capacity_model_v1)

Let me know if you want a short simulation export (tokens/sec timeline) I can attach to the quote.

- Priyom

Thanks Maya — this is super helpful. Quick summary of what we'll include in the Dedicated proposal and the operational commitments we'll bake into the SOW: 

- Capacity plan (proposal):
  - Reserved: 4 quantized slabs in us-west-2 (covers steady-state and short growth).
  - Autoscale policy: scale up to 10 quantized slabs for short spikes (policy triggers on token/sec windows); pre-warm KV cache during scheduled batch windows.
  - FP16 fallback: 2 FP16 slabs for long-tail 1,800-token jobs.
  - Safety margin: 25% cushion included in quote pricing for the first 3 months.

- SLOs & routing: p95 <= 200ms for user routes (we'll instrument routing policies to failover to FP16 pool if quantized slabs breach latency thresholds).

- Network/peering: propose direct interconnect in us-west-2; procurement can follow up with the peering order (I copied them on this thread).

Attachments: anchorage_capacity_model_v1.xlsx (detailed scenarios), peering-diagram.png (recommended topology). I also attached a short tokens/sec simulation if you'd like a CSV export — Priyom, could you generate that and I will surface in the quote?

If this looks good, let's schedule a 30-min alignment with procurement and engineering tomorrow; I'll prepare a draft SOW and a DocuSign for the initial commitment (link below).
